clue.text: Fabric cut in back and put on view

indicators.note: a cut word has been trimmed, so its final letter is lopped off
going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
to air something is to display it publicly

explanation.surface: Someone trims a piece of cloth at the back and then puts it on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a mere preposition, but it stands for HOME; cut to HOM and turned back it becomes MOH, followed by AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a soft cloth woven from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Celtic characters in hotel try rolls before noon

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns upside down, so in a down clue the letters run backwards

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet
to have a go is to have a try
a.m. means before midday

explanation.surface: A hotel guest trying bread rolls before lunchtime, with some Celtic lettering thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' reads as bread rolls, but in a down clue it is the instruction to turn the hotel and the try upside down; 'in' merely joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is the ancient alphabet of strokes used for inscriptions in early Irish and British stones.

clue.text: Sailor in a hurry to accommodate Irish, improving image

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room inside, so one part sits within another

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
IR is the standard abbreviation for Irish
someone in a hurry is rushing

explanation.surface: A sailor rushing to make room for an Irishman, perhaps on a crowded ship, while working on his public image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor in' seems to belong together, but AB takes in IR to make AIRB, and 'in a hurry' is RUSHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Airbrushing is retouching a photograph to remove flaws, so it literally improves a picture or someone's public appearance.

clue.text: Run over by Hulot’s creator on cycle

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
Jacques Tati created the comic character Monsieur Hulot
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked down by the French film-maker who created Monsieur Hulot while he rides a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' looks like a traffic accident, but it is two cricket abbreviations. Monsieur Hulot is the bumbling hero of Jacques Tati's films, in which Tati himself rides a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation is a regular repeating sequence or turn, just as a cycle comes round again and again.

clue.text: Vase from Parma smashed outside little house

indicators.note: something smashed lies in broken pieces, so these letters are rearranged
to be outside something is to surround it, so one set wraps around another

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
HO is the short form of house

explanation.surface: An Italian vase from Parma has been smashed outside a small cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: PARMA is shuffled to AMPRA and HO, the abbreviation for house, is placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled ancient Greek or Roman jar, a type of tall vessel.

clue.text: Vikings heading down to the middle Peak District

indicators.note: the front letter travels down into the centre, so it is placed inside what remains

blocks.note: the Vikings were Danes and other Scandinavians

explanation.surface: Viking raiders marching down into the middle of Derbyshire's Peak District.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'heading' of DANES is its first letter D; moving it down into the middle gives AN-D-ES. 'Peak District' looks like the English national park but means any region of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes is the great South American mountain range, a whole district of peaks, cheekily described with an English place name.

clue.text: Board has power replacing leading trio in film industry

indicators.note: replacing the first three letters means swapping them out for something new

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power
Hollywood is the home of the American film industry

explanation.surface: A board of directors gains power in the movie business.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLLYWOOD loses its first three letters HOL, and P takes their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Plywood is building board made from thin glued layers of timber.

clue.text: Pleasant-smelling rose our Fido chewed

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The family dog has chewed up a sweet-smelling rose from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog, which makes 'chewed' natural in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Odoriferous means giving off a scent, so a fragrant flower is the perfect example.

clue.text: Stories about sappers in scene of conflict

indicators.note: about means around, so one part wraps another

blocks.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
the Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers, are the RE

explanation.surface: Tales told of army engineers serving in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a crossword favourite for a collection of stories, goes about RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest, originally where gladiators fought, so any scene of struggle.

clue.text: Performance tribal leader captured initially in recording

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only
in places one group inside the other

blocks.note: Dan was the founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel
the first letter of captured
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A performance in which a tribal chief was caught on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tribal leader' wants to be a first letter T, but it is the biblical patriarch Dan, founder of the tribe of Israel that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap dance is a stage routine performed in shoes with metal plates.

clue.text: Disagreed also with a thousand children

blocks.note: too means also
K stands for a thousand
issue is offspring, in legal language

explanation.surface: Someone also objected to having a thousand children.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue is the formal word for a person's children, as in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with something is to dispute it, an idiom for voicing disagreement.

clue.text: Page covering mathematical sequence

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
a roof is a covering

explanation.surface: A page that covers a mathematical series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' looks like a container instruction, but it simply gives ROOF after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical proof is a chain of logical steps leading to a conclusion, so it is a sequence of reasoning.

clue.text: Surprise with ear affected when this changes?

definitions.text: Surprise with ear affected when this changes?

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed in order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller is surprised to find their ears affected by something changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: SURPRISE and EAR are mixed up, and the clue as a whole describes the popping ears felt on a plane or in a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: When atmospheric force changes quickly, as on take-off, the eardrums feel it, an unpleasant surprise to many travellers.

clue.text: Ranch hand from old west quietly immersed in drink

indicators.note: to be immersed is to be plunged into, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
W is the abbreviation for west
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
Coke is a soft drink

explanation.surface: A cowboy from the Wild West quietly sinking into his whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old west' reads as the Wild West, but it is two abbreviations, O and W, joined by P and then sunk inside COKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowpoke is American slang for a cowboy, a hired worker who herds cattle.

clue.text: Individual in grotty aerodrome who contrived to be short-lived

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: one is a single individual
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a shabby airfield schemed to make something not last.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE joins the eighteen letters of 'grotty aerodrome who' and all twenty-one are rearranged. Grotty is British slang for shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes anything fleeting that vanishes as quickly as it came, so it works as an idiom for transient.

clue.text: Retired Hull partner’s holding tax for return

indicators.note: returning means going back, so these letters run the other way
holding something means having it inside, so one part sits in another

blocks.note: Emu was the puppet partner of the comedian Rod Hull; with the 's
to tax someone is to tire them out

explanation.surface: A retired business partner from Hull is holding on to a tax refund.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire city, but it is Rod Hull, a British TV entertainer whose stage partner was a hand puppet called Emu. EMU'S holds TIRE reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor or official who has stepped down but keeps an honorary title.

clue.text: Love doctor, Nancy’s friend, modelling in paper

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to doctor results is to rig them
ami is French for friend, and Nancy is a French city

explanation.surface: A romantic doctor, a friend of a woman named Nancy, poses for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name, but it is the city in north-east France, so its friend is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding sheets into decorative shapes, a craft of making figures from folded sheets.

clue.text: Quarrel coming after fine for litter

indicators.note: coming after places one part behind another in the line

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: An argument that follows a fine for dropping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' wants to be ROW, but that leaves FAR unexplained; it is the crossbow bolt, the archer's sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is a litter of piglets, the young born to a sow at one time.

clue.text: Visits duke declines

blocks.note: to visit someone is to go to see them
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A nobleman turns down an invitation to call on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declines' reads as refuses in the surface, but it means deteriorates.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed has stopped flowering, so the idiom describes a person or place falling into shabbiness.

clue.text: Stubborn stain to be treated

indicators.note: something treated has been processed and changed, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A stubborn mark on a carpet that needs cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stubborn stain' is a stock phrase from detergent adverts, which hides that 'Stubborn' is the definition and 'to be' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person refuses to change their mind, which is exactly what being headstrong means.

clue.text: Example chapter taken from long story book

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
an epic is a long narrative poem or tale
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A sample chapter lifted out of a lengthy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Example' looks like part of the surface's sample chapter, but it is the definition; the long story is a classical-style tale whose chapter letter is lifted out.
explanation.definitionFit: The epitome of something is its perfect embodiment, the ideal instance that typifies a whole class.

clue.text: Ridiculously lively press surrounding English or US icon

indicators.note: ridiculously means absurdly, so the letters are thrown into a silly new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An excited press pack swarms around an English star, or an American one.
explanation.walkthrough: E is added to LIVELY PRESS, and all twelve letters are shuffled; 'surrounding' tells you the E goes in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, the King of Rock and Roll, is one of the most famous American cultural figures.

clue.text: Philistine victory over European initially reduced

indicators.note: reduced at the start means its first letter is cut off

blocks.note: V is the sign and abbreviation for victory
a Bulgarian is a European

explanation.surface: A biblical Philistine wins a battle over a European who is cut down at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places V on top in a down clue. 'Philistine' suggests Goliath's people, but here it means someone without taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is someone hostile to culture, and a vulgarian is a coarse person of poor taste.

clue.text: Editor’s job to conceal Democrat opposition to political change

indicators.note: concealing something means making it disappear from view, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: redaction is the editing of a text for publication
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: An editor is tasked with hiding a Democrat's resistance to political reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Redaction is also the blacking out of sensitive text, so 'conceal' fits the surface while telling you to remove the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaction in politics is resistance to progress or reform, the stance of the reactionary.

clue.text: Wine in a small container any number refused

indicators.note: something refused is turned away, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
a tin is a container
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: Wine served in a little container that any number of people turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the mathematician's unspecified number, is dropped from TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white from Piedmont, named after the town where it is made.

clue.text: One active in small hours close to lough, drinking whiskey

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the rest

blocks.note: nigh means near or close
taken as written
W is Whiskey in the NATO alphabet
L is the map abbreviation for lake or lough

explanation.surface: Someone up in the early hours near an Irish lake, drinking whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like a last-letter instruction, but 'close' is NIGH and 'to' stands for itself. A lough is an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who habitually stays up late, like the nocturnal bird.

clue.text: Superior-sounding structure unknown in priesthood

indicators.note: sounding means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: superior means higher
an arch is a built structure
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding building of mysterious origin in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: HIER is not a word but a spelling that says 'higher' aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Hierarchy originally meant the ranked order of clergy, and still names a church's body of priests.

clue.text: Assess empty learner replacing academic at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only
replacing means one letter is swapped for another in its place

blocks.note: to empty a building is to evacuate it
L is the learner plate
the last letter of academic

explanation.surface: Judging a student who has no work in him, as he takes an academic's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty learner' looks like a person with nothing to offer, but 'empty' is a verb giving EVACUATE. The L plate marks a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to weigh up or judge the worth of something, which is what assessing means.

clue.text: Drink repercussions disheartened sleuth must accept

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter
to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: tec is short for detective
ripples are spreading after-effects

explanation.surface: A dejected detective has to face the consequences of his drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tec' is old slang for a detective; the after-effects lose one of their two middle letters before being taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is a clear orange-flavoured liqueur used in cocktails such as the margarita.

clue.text: Bear left turning for city and borough there?

indicators.note: turning round sends the letters in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to brook is to bear or tolerate
L is the abbreviation for left
NY is New York; 'for' gives the city

explanation.surface: A bear heads off, turning toward the city and its district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is a verb. 'there' points back to the city, so the definition is a borough of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five administrative districts that make up New York City.

clue.text: Spice received by South American celebrity

blocks.note: ginger is a spice
Roger is radio-speak for message received
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A spice imported by a South American star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase, but South gives S and American belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Rogers was a Hollywood actress and dancer, famous as Fred Astaire's partner.

clue.text: Opposition from MI6 on a new tax

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so one piece follows another

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tithe is a tenth paid as a levy
MI6 is Britain's Secret Intelligence Service, the SIS

explanation.surface: The spy agency objects to a newly introduced tax.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence service, officially the Secret Intelligence Service; 'on' puts it after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is a direct contrast or opposite, the counter-position to a thesis.

clue.text: News items Henry substituted with primitive thoughts

indicators.note: substituted with means swapped out for something else in the same place

blocks.note: items are things
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
the id is the instinctive part of the mind in Freudian theory

explanation.walkthrough: 'News items' reads as one phrase, but 'News' is the definition and 'items' is THINGS, whose H gives way to the Freudian ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or reports, as in 'glad tidings'.

clue.text: CIA ensnaring fool, minor poet occasionally following stars

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept
following means coming after, so one piece is placed behind another
ensnaring means trapping inside, so one group goes within another

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
the even letters of minor poet
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The CIA is split around the fool and the even letters of 'minor poet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassiopeia is a W-shaped constellation in the northern sky, a group of stars named after a queen of Greek myth.

clue.text: Vote to have cards on display?

blocks.note: first meaning: a vote taken by people raising their arms
second meaning, playful: card players laying down what they hold

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, in which a hand is the set of cards each player holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote by raised arms is the literal sense, and card players revealing what they hold is the punning one.

clue.text: Eventually stop throat gland twitching — after one’s swallowed?

indicators.note: twitching means jerking about, so the letters move into a new order
swallowed means taken inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A throat gland keeps twitching after someone has swallowed, until it finally settles.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is taken into the jumble of 'throat gland', so all twelve letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind to a halt is to slow gradually until movement ceases, like a machine running down.

clue.text: Board game — single punter to excel

blocks.note: Go is the Japanese board game played with stones
single means one
a punter is a gambler, one who bets

explanation.surface: A board game in which a lone gambler aims to shine.
explanation.walkthrough: A punter is British slang for someone placing a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To go one better is an idiom for outdoing someone, surpassing what they have achieved.

clue.text: Composer one carrying can ultimately appearing in Private Eye

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
appearing in means showing up inside, so one letter sits within another word

blocks.note: to hump is to carry something heavy, so a carrier is a humper
a private eye is a detective, slang dick
the last letter of can

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye looks like the British satirical magazine, but it is a detective, slang dick. Engelbert Humperdinck wrote the opera Hansel and Gretel.
explanation.definitionFit: Engelbert Humperdinck was a German writer of music, best known for the fairy-tale opera Hansel and Gretel.

clue.text: Changes appearance of tyres given new tread

blocks.note: first meaning: reshapes
second meaning: retreaded tyres

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about tyres, but it splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To remould is to shape again, and a remould is a worn tyre with a fresh rubber surface bonded on.

clue.text: Playwright parking in London area, indications centrally ignored

indicators.note: in places one letter inside another word
ignoring the centre means dropping the middle letter

blocks.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
Soho is a district of central London
clues are indications or hints

explanation.walkthrough: Soho is the theatre and nightlife district of London's West End; CLUES loses its middle letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was an ancient Greek tragedian, author of Oedipus Rex and Antigone.

clue.text: Conservative having to accept Liberal’s acting the fool

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
having something means owning it
L is the abbreviation for Liberal; the following 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A Tory forced to take on a Liberal politician is making a fool of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' looks like a link word, but it gives OWNING, and C plus OWNING takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowning is fooling around like a circus jester, behaving comically or foolishly.

clue.text: Not seen: heard in fog

indicators.note: heard means as caught by the ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: something not seen has been missed

explanation.surface: Something unseen but audible in thick fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and 'heard' make the surface sound like a ghost story; 'missed' and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a thin haze of water droplets, a lighter form of fog.

clue.text: Left for Romans, most of Greek wine is revolting

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
revolting means turning over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: retsina is a resin-flavoured Greek wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman complains that most Greek wine tastes disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting but it turns RETSIN plus IS backwards. In Latin, sinister simply meant on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is the Latin word for the left-hand side, which is why heraldry still uses it that way.

clue.text: Story always having to go round for cheque’s intended recipient

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped by another

blocks.note: an account is a story or report
to go is a coy euphemism for urinating

clue.text: German poet loses head, seeing horror film

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

blocks.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist

explanation.surface: A German poet is decapitated, as in a scary movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Schiller wrote the Ode to Joy used in Beethoven's Ninth; his S goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiller is a frightening story or movie, one that sends a shiver down the spine.

clue.text: Avoidance, or non-appearance, to include time at home?

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so one group goes inside another

blocks.note: not appearing is absence
T is the abbreviation for time
someone at home is in

clue.text: True: sea can be cold

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An observation that the ocean really can be chilly.

explanation.definitionFit: An austere manner is stern and severe, lacking warmth, just as a cold person is.

clue.text: Endlessly dreadful meat that makes change in Casablanca?

ham is a meat

clue.text: Low note in brass

la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

clue.text: Egyptian god leaving horse outside pub with eastern bard

clue.text: Silver penny no longer in circulation?

clue.text: Important way alpha male does twirl wearing women’s clothes

blocks.note: A is Alpha in the NATO alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: 'alpha male' is a stock phrase, but it splits into two abbreviations, spun round.
explanation.definitionFit: A main drag is the chief street of a town, a slang term for the principal thoroughfare.

clue.text: First and second swapping places, getting damp

1st, with the 1 read as I

clue.text: States not entirely hostile

explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert firmly, so someone who avers a fact states it.

clue.text: Easiest way Allies often organised underground fighters

explanation.surface: In the war the Allies often set up secret resistance cells behind enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' seems to describe the fighters but rearranges the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the course requiring least effort, like water flowing where it meets least opposition.

clue.text: Lock spring breaks to give uninvited access

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A sprung lock gives way, letting in an intruder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock spring' reads as a door mechanism, but the lock is hair and the spring is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is the unlawful entry onto someone else's land without their permission.

clue.text: On about knight buried in card player’s grave

indicators.note: something buried is sunk inside, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: re means on or about, as in a memo
N is the chess notation for knight
East is one of the four players at bridge; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone goes on about a knight who lies buried in a card player's tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a tomb, but it is the adjective for solemn. In bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and sincere in manner, just as a grave look is solemn.

clue.text: Debauched son initially hooked on strong Levantine booze

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: raki is a strong anise spirit from Turkey and the eastern Mediterranean
S is the abbreviation for son
the first letter of hooked

explanation.surface: A dissolute son became addicted to strong eastern spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the first part after the second, so the drink comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakish person behaves like a rake, a dissolute man of loose morals.
